title: Config Sensitivity Matrix and Shadow Probe Harness for Embedding-Reranker Regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: config and model variant changes (quantization profiles, caching policies, batch sizing, and reranker threshold tweaks) have produced intermittent embedding/rerank quality regressions in customer cohorts. We need a repeatable, automated offline evaluation + shadow-probe harness to measure sensitivity to config changes and reliably gate changes before rollout.

Scope: build a Config Sensitivity Matrix generator and a Shadow Probe runner that executes on config/model change events (PRs or config push). The system will: (1) select representative cohorts and holdouts, (2) run offline recall@k/precision@k, MRR, and embedding distribution drift checks, (3) compute a sensitivity score per change and per cohort, (4) surface results in an eval dashboard and create an automated gate decision (pass/warn/block) with evidence.

Out of scope: online A/B infrastructure or full integration with canary traffic (those will follow after this gate blocks are stable).
acceptance_criteria: Automated job runs on config/model change events and finishes within SLA (typically < 60 minutes for nightly full-run, < 15 minutes for quick smoke run)
Generates Config Sensitivity Matrix CSV and JSON artefacts that list delta metrics per cohort and per metric
Defines tunable thresholds (recall@10 drop > 2pt or JS divergence > 0.06) that result in PASS/WARN/BLOCK decisions
Integrates results into eval dashboard with links to raw artifacts, sample failing queries, and stable baseline snapshots
Produces a GitHub PR comment summary with key deltas and a link to the full report
Has a lightweight rollback recommendation stub that can be extended by release automation
runbook: Trigger: webhook on model/config change or manual run from CLI
Quick path: smoke-run (sampled cohorts, top-1000 queries) => target time < 15 minutes
Full path: full-run (stratified cohorts, holdouts, multi-seed reranker) => target time < 60 minutes
Decision rules: compare baseline snapshot (tagged) to new outputs; apply delta thresholds to compute PASS/WARN/BLOCK
Failure handling: on BLOCK, artifact links and representative failing queries are posted to PR and to #eng-embed-regressions; create rollback ticket if auto-rollback is enabled
Escalation: if high customer_impact or > 5% query failures, page on-call infra lead
comments: 2026-01-28 | Asha Patel: Created ticket after a retail customer reported a subtle drop in top-5 relevance following a quantization profile change. Initial triage indicates distribution drift rather than infra errors.

2026-02-03 | Marco Gomez: PoC of sensitivity matrix generator finished. PoC computes recall deltas and outputs per-cohort CSV. Observed two cohorts with recall@10 drops > 3pts for the quantized variant.

2026-02-10 | Kira Zhang (review): Proposed adding JS divergence on embedding distributions and a small sample of human-labeled checks (20 queries/cohort) for high-impact changes. Also suggested quick smoke run and full-run modes.

2026-02-18 | Marco Gomez: Implemented embedding JS divergence computation and cohort sampling framework. Updated thresholds: recall@10 drop > 2.0 => WARN, > 4.0 => BLOCK; JS divergence > 0.06 => WARN. Pushed initial dashboard panel.
2026-02-24 | PR #214: infra-evals changes submitted for review (link above). Code reviewers asked for determinism in sampling; added seed control and stored seeds in artifacts for reproducibility.

2026-03-02 | ML QA (Priya Rao): Ran smoke-run on runtime-1.24 with heavy reranker seeds; found unstable MRR for one policy. Added a follow-up ENG subtask to instrument per-request reranker logs for the failing cohort.
2026-03-08 | Security (review): Confirmed no PII in sampled queries; artifact storage access needs to be restricted to eng and SRE roles. Added s3 bucket policy task.

2026-03-10 | Marco Gomez: Smoke-run results attached to ticket; sensitivity matrix shows one BLOCK due to recall@10 drop of 5.1 pts in 'marketing-search' cohort for quantized-8bit profile. Next: widen holdout, run full-run, and prepare customer impact analysis.
notes: Trade-offs: fast smoke runs might miss long-tail regressions; full-run is slower and more costly. We'll use a tiered approach: smoke-run gate + nightly full-run for high-risk changes.
Implementation detail: use parquet artifacts, store seeds and baseline tags, and add hash of config diff to artifact metadata so results are traceable to exact change.
Decision: start with offline gating (PR comments + dashboard) before wiring into automated CI blocks. The goal is to gather signal and avoid noisy false-positives.
Follow-ups: integrate canary online checks and auto-rollback in subsequent sprint; add synthetic adversarial probes to surface brittle reranker behavior.
